text:
omar: Heads up — we've been seeing a spike in preemptible interruption rates in europe-west1 between 20:00-00:00 UTC for the last 3 nights. Interactive latency SLOs are getting noisy.

sasha: Yep noticed that too. Batch queues mostly fine but interactive jobs (notebook / playground) get killed mid-session.

maria: Any correlation with large nightly training/batch windows? Could be greedy batch stealing capacity.

kevin: Looking at autoscaler logs: a lot of spot churn + node termination waves at ~20:15. Autoscaler retries but pods lose warm kv cache.

omar: We should consider a short-term mitigation: route interactive to a small on-demand pool during evening hours and keep batch on preemptible with tighter packing. Cost hit but keeps customer UX. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

li: Agreed. Proposed quick plan:
- carve out 10% of the fleet as evening-reserved on-demand (policy hour range)
- lower batch scheduler weight for interactive-critical projects
- increase preemptible grace period to 90s for checkpointing where supported

maria: Can we do smarter scoring instead of blunt carve? e.g., priority-steering that prefers nodes with lower recent interruption scores + instance-lifetime filter. That would keep more capacity on spot but reduce user-visible impact.

kevin: We have telemetry to compute interruption_rate(node) over rolling 6h. Could add to nodeSelector score quickly. Example:

```yaml
priorityScore: base_priority - (interruption_weight * interruption_rate)
```

sasha: Also recommend adding an interactive queue preemption policy: allow 30s to attempt graceful checkpoint then migrate to sticky fallback route -> launch small model on on-demand pool or proxy to cached completion. Minimizes full session loss.

omar: Good. Let's be explicit about rollout: 1) today 20:00-00:00 reserve 10% on-demand cap for 7 days, 2) deploy node scoring change to staging, 3) enable interactive preempt behavior and monitor error budget.

devops-bot: autoscaler: created 12 on-demand nodes (eu-west1) for policy window 20:00-00:00 UTC — TTL 7d.

li: I'll open a small runtime PR for scoring and preempt hooks. Keeping changes toggleable via feature flag. PR in: https://git.redwood/mock/pull/321 :thumbsup:

maria: We'll need a quick cost estimate for the 10% reserve. Back-of-envelope: current spot spend in eu-west1 ~ $6k/day; 10% on-demand uplift ~ ~$600/day extra. I'll post detailed calc.

kevin: Also add metric: user-session-abandon rate for interactive between 19:45-00:15. Rollback if abandonment goes up.

omar: Thanks team. Action items: li PR, kevin add session abandonment dashboard, maria cost calc, sasha prepare preempt hook behavior doc. We'll reconvene tomorrow 09:30 to review staging signals.

sasha: one more note — check network egress quotas in eu-west1; past nights we also hit a transient NAT gateway throttle causing pod restarts. Might be compounding the problem.

omar: Good catch. kevin can you confirm NAT error spikes in logs?

kevin: Confirmed — ~30% more 5xx egress errors at 20:10-20:25. I'll add NAT throttling to the checklist.

maria: Great. If the 7d test looks good, we should make a quarterly off-peak policy: shift some batch to earlier window and increase interactive protection window in region config.

li: PR opened and flagged for review. I'll include fallback route code snippet and small sim harness to validate checkpoint+restore flow.

omar: Perfect. I'll update the runbook with the temp policy and notify support/ux. Thanks everyone :rocket:
